  • VDD: centre y = 6 um, thickness at least 0.23 um, from left + 0 um to right − 0 um.
  • VSS: centre y = 0.35 um, thickness at least 0.23 um, from left + 0 um to right − 0 um.

Electrical Requirements and Scoring

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Quality scoring imposes no fixed degradation allowance. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. Independent source observations remain required evidence; the quality targets below set the scoring anchors without depending on the submitted GDS. Reports retain every source/candidate pair.

Let x be the post-layout measurement and b the declared quality target, or the same-condition source measurement when no target is declared:

  • Ratio normalization: maximize with q = x/b and minimize with q = b/x. When a numerical scale s is declared, use (x+s)/(b+s) and its reciprocal, respectively. The scale handles zero values as a normalization floor; it is neither an allowed degradation nor an acceptance bound.
  • Amplitude in dB: maximize with q = 10^((x-b)/20) and minimize with its reciprocal.
  • Target normalization: q = 1/(1+abs(x-b)/s), where s is the declared physical scale. Signed or zero-valued operating points are not divided directly.

Use layout scoring. First compute each metric's raw quality q from the worst paired condition, with raw area quality q_area = area_target / candidate_functional_area. Credit c_i = min(1, q_i) for every positively weighted metric, then compute S = 100 * product(c_i ** w_i). The weights sum to 1 and the score is bounded by 100. An improvement beyond one target cannot compensate for missing another target. Physical or functional rejection scores zero; missing or invalid measurements leave the score unknown, and zero-weight observations must also be valid. Reaching every positively weighted target scores 100; a feasible reference may score far below 100. Weights express quality tradeoffs, not acceptance bounds.

Metric Definition / observation Unit Quality normalization Functional range Scale
low Q at 19, 59, 89, 99 and 139 ns plus the 191.5 ns near-edge capture/hold check; the 89 ns sample checks asynchronous reset before the next rising clock. V functional check −∞ … 0.33 —
high Q at 39, 79 and 119 ns plus the 151.5 ns near-edge capture/hold check, exercising functional and scan data. V functional check 2.97 … +∞ —
propagation_delay Worst paired quality over the five existing data/scan/reset arcs and two additional A-data clock-to-Q arcs with 0.8 ns setup. s minimize / ratio 0 … +∞ —
output_transition Worst paired quality over the five existing data/scan/reset arcs and the two additional A-data output-slew arcs with 0.8 ns setup. s minimize / ratio 0 … +∞ —
supply Average VDD power over 20–200 ns, including the late-cycle timing stimuli. W minimize / ratio 0 … +∞ 1e-12

The area scoring target is 100 um2. It is a continuous quality goal, not a hard limit, process minimum or a percentage of the current feasibility witness.

  • propagation_delay: 5.5e-10 s. Keep all declared clock/data/reset-to-Q timing observations within 550 ps at 50 fF, including the late-cycle capture exercises.

The 100 um2 area goal rewards compact latch, clock and scan-multiplexer placement. Timing 45% and area 40% expose clock/internal-node routing cost, with 10% slew and 5% power. The 550 ps target is close to the slowest source path. Fixed setup/hold exercises establish correct capture, not a characterized minimum setup or hold time.

Quality targets do not impose additional functional cutoffs. Metrics without an explicit target retain their same-condition source anchors.

The capability coefficient is 5, independent of this task's reference-normalized score.

Standard-cell design guidance

You may plan device rows, supply rails and signal access before routing. Represent pull-up/pull-down connections as transistor-edge graphs and explore compatible Euler paths and alternative orders to share diffusion and reduce breaks. Choose a legal arrangement considering routing length, parasitics and signal access. Keep fixed netlist sizes, models and connections; do not optimize sizing.

Use the declared row height, grid and supply-rail geometry. Keep local routing compact and signal pins accessible, avoiding routing layers with no benefit. Check DRC and named-port LVS, then extract the candidate and compare transitions in both directions and power against source simulation; iterate using parasitic measurements. These methods are optional and do not prescribe an algorithm or reference layout.

These methods refer to Sections 2–3 of Xu et al., Standard Cell Library Design and Optimization Methodology for ASAP7 PDK (https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.11396). Its FinFET sizing, track count and process-specific dimensions do not apply to this task.

Metric Weight
functional_area 0.4
propagation_delay 0.45
output_transition 0.1
supply 0.05

CMOS Inverter Threshold Core Layout Task

Objective

The fixed binding is a CMOS inverter: one 1/0.13 um NMOS and one 2.5/0.13 um PMOS, each m=1. Bodies connect to their respective rails through native physical contacts. It provides a threshold decision core; there is no sampling, independent reference, encoding or complete ADC. Target top cell: adc_001_inv1b.

Inputs and Interface

materials/circuit.cdl is the authoritative logical circuit netlist; materials/circuit.spice is the same compact-device circuit for simulation. materials/testbench.spice supplies the external fixture. Both source and extracted candidate use the exact same deck, bias, loads, excitation, initial-state procedure and measurement windows. Ordered ports: vdd (1.2 V rail), vin (gate input), vout (drain output), vss (return).

Operating Conditions

IHP LV MOS TT, 27 C, VDD=1.2 V. Input driver impedance is 50 ohm; output capacitance is 20 fF. DC input sweeps 0–1.2 V in 1 mV steps. The transient driver starts at 0 V, rises at 10 ns, falls at 20.1 ns, has 100 ps edges and a 20 ns period. The initial DC output is high. The 31 ns run uses a maximum 1 ps step. Power is the net energy from supply and input driver divided by the 10–30 ns window.

Physical Requirements

Use IHP native KLayout main and maximum rule decks and named-interface LVS; Magic full RC extraction. No case-specific waivers. Candidate extraction must preserve every model, multiplicity, size, resistor value, connection and ordered port. The functional outline includes devices, wells, contacts and all routing layers declared in the public task; annotation and pin labels do not add area. Maximum outline: 5000 by 1000 um. Maximum GDS size: 10485760 bytes. Every device and resistor must be physical; no ideal internal macro or auxiliary servo may be added. External sources, probe loads and storage capacitors belong to the testbench.

Electrical Requirements and Scoring

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Quality scoring imposes no fixed degradation allowance. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. Independent source observations define the 100-point electrical baseline without depending on the submitted GDS; reports retain every paired result.

Let x be the post-layout measurement and b the source-circuit measurement under the same conditions:

  • Ratio normalization: maximize with q = x/b and minimize with q = b/x. When a numerical scale s is declared, use (x+s)/(b+s) and its reciprocal, respectively. The scale handles zero values as a normalization floor; it is neither an allowed degradation nor an acceptance bound.
  • Amplitude in dB: maximize with q = 10^((x-b)/20) and minimize with its reciprocal.
  • Target normalization: q = 1/(1+abs(x-b)/s), where s is the declared physical scale. Signed or zero-valued operating points are not divided directly.

Use layout scoring. Each metric takes its worst paired quality q, and the total score is S = 100 * product(q_i ** w_i), with area quality q_area = area_reference / candidate_functional_area. The weights below sum to 1; metric dimensions describe measurements and do not determine weights. Physical or functional rejection scores zero; missing or invalid measurements leave the score unknown, and zero-weight observations must also be valid. Matching source-circuit performance at the reference area scores 100 points; better valid solutions may exceed 100. Weights express quality tradeoffs rather than hard bounds.

Metric Unit Definition Bound Quality
threshold_v V Unique DC output=0.6 V crossing unbounded to unbounded response: target, target, scale=0.6
delay_s s Worst 50% input to opposite 50% output delay 0 to unbounded response: ratio, minimize, scale=1e-12
transition_s s Worst output 10–90% or 90–10% transition 0 to unbounded response: ratio, minimize, scale=1e-12
power_w W Mean net supply and input-driver power from 10–30 ns 0 to unbounded supply: ratio, minimize, scale=1e-12
swing_v V DC high minus low output; meaningful logic transition 0.6 to unbounded diagnostic / functional only

The DC threshold is the unique output=0.6 V crossing, not a scan endpoint. Delay is the worse input 50% to opposite output 50% delay. Transition is the worse output 10–90% rise or 90–10% fall. Guards reject missing or multiple DC/transition crossings; independent audits require the intended 10–15 ns and 20–25 ns windows and correct ordering. DC high/low output uses actual endpoint samples, with a minimum 0.6 V swing establishing a meaningful logic transition. This is nominal loaded characterization, not Liberty/PVT or ADC accuracy.

Static output bounds check the corresponding supply domain; nonnegative power/error conditions define the measurement domain; KCL checks reject inconsistent DC solutions. Every condition must be valid; upstream advertised performance is not a hard threshold. The metric table declares target scales and normalization floors; floors handle zero-error ratios, and neither scales nor floors are acceptance tolerances.

Each metric uses the worst source-paired quality over matching conditions. Target quality is 1/(1+abs(candidate-source)/scale), and minimizing ratio quality is (source+scale)/(candidate+scale). Missing, nonfinite or invalid source/candidate measurements and tool failures make the score unknown; confirmed physical/functional rejection scores zero. Gates apply separately to every observation.

Compact area anchor: 120 um2 = 20 um2 NMOS contact envelope + 30 um2 PMOS/well envelope + 20 um2 body-contact/isolation allowance + 50 um2 routing. These envelopes follow the fixed widths and contact/isolation needs, not the witness bounding box. Coefficient 1: a single logic stage with loaded transitions and connectivity. Objective

Implement the fixed six-MOS amp_001_5t circuit in IHP SG13G2 and submit a self-contained GDS. The circuit consists of a five-transistor OTA core and a sixth, diode-connected bias-reference MOS. Device dimensions are fixed.

Inputs and Interface

Current-Buffer and Active-Feedforward OTA Layout Task

Objective

Lay out amp_002_alfio_raffc with its physical compensation and fixed transistor network, for the declared loop response and sustained unity-feedback step recovery.

The folded PMOS-input stage drives net050; a PMOS common-source stage drives net013, then a PMOS stage and NMOS mirror at net043 drive the output NMOS. An active feedforward path drives the output PMOS directly from net050. One capacitor connects output to net063, the source side of the first-stage NMOS cascode; the second connects net050 to net013. The current-buffer compensation terminal and the additional active path are real connection differences from the dual-capacitor and shared-resistor representatives. This case is not counted from a changed circuit name or size.

The maintained circuit retains all 24 source MOS groups as 89 physical fingers, 4 MIM units and 0 high-poly segments. MOS W/L are rounded to the nearest 0.01 um process grid. The original W=18/20/30 um devices use 2×9/2×10/3×10 um parallel fingers; the resulting short-width model behavior is calibrated independently. The source's 14.3293 uA sink is external through net1. Physical substrate and separate N-well contacts retain the input PMOS bodies at their common source net31, electrically separate from the VDD well. No internal ideal bias source or output servo is introduced. Capacitor values are rounded to physical geometry; every branch remains internal to the DUT.

Inputs and Interface

  • materials/circuit.cdl: authoritative native LVS circuit.
  • materials/circuit.spice: simulation circuit bound to the process models.

Input PMOS bodies retain the separate source-tied well; other PMOS bodies use the VDD well and NMOS bodies use the VSS substrate contact. Preserve device W/L/m, body connectivity, all internal branches and total multiplicities in the authoritative netlist. Native equivalent parallel fingers are allowed only when LVS and electrical requirements pass. Do not short distinct ports or create extra driven monitors.

Internal passive devices are listed below; external loads are declared separately:

  • c0: net063 → vout, 3 parallel cap_cmim unit(s), each 43.46 × 43.46 um; nominal total 8.520333 pF.
  • c1: net050 → net013, 1 parallel cap_cmim unit(s), each 36.515 × 36.515 um; nominal total 2.0058602 pF.

The maintained circuit retains all 24 source MOS groups as 89 physical fingers, 4 MIM units and 0 high-poly segments. MOS W/L are rounded to the nearest 0.01 um process grid. The folded PMOS-input stage drives net050; a PMOS/diode/mirror stage drives net049, followed by the NMOS output stage. A parallel path drives the output PMOS directly from net050. One capacitor connects net049 to output. The other connects output to net1, the source terminal of an additional common-gate NMOS returning current to net050. Six additional MOS (XM59–XM64) form this biased current-buffer branch; these devices and the low-impedance compensation terminal distinguish it from direct Miller and shared-resistor compensation.

The maintained circuit retains all 30 source MOS groups as 276 physical fingers, 7 MIM units and 0 high-poly segments. MOS W/L are rounded to the nearest 0.01 um process grid. All source multiplicities are retained. The maintained 3.15498 uA sink is external through net013. The external bias is deliberately calibrated to 0.3 times the source current; this is not an unchanged upstream operating point. Physical substrate and separate N-well contacts retain the input PMOS bodies at their common source net31, electrically separate from the VDD well. No internal ideal bias source or output servo is introduced. Capacitor values are rounded to physical geometry; every branch remains internal to the DUT.
sections.Operating Conditions:
Use typical MOS/MIM/poly models at 27 C, VDD=1.2 V and the declared external bias. All three output loads, 5/10/20 pF, must pass. At DC, VINP=0.5 V and VOUT feeds back to VINN through a zero-volt measurement source. For AC, inject 1 V in series with the feedback connection and set VINP AC=0; the return ratio at the high-impedance MOS input boundary is T=-V(vout)/V(vm). Sweep 150 points per decade from 0.01 Hz to 100 MHz with continuous phase, without arbitrary correction of the low-frequency phase offset. The first falling 0 dB crossing defines unity-gain frequency, and 180+phase(T) at that crossing defines phase margin. A missing crossing is an evaluation error.

VINP rises from 0.5 V to 0.7 V during 2–2.02 us and falls during 10.02–10.04 us, repeating every 16 us. Simulate 0–18 us with second-order Gear, a maximum step of 2 ns, rshunt=1e12, reltol=1e-5, abstol=1e-14 and vntol=1e-8. Numerical shunt branches are not physical bias or startup devices. PVT, mismatch, noise, distortion, rail-to-rail operation, power-up and stability under arbitrary loads are outside scope.
sections.Physical Requirements:
Submit GDSII top cell amp_005_hoilee_affc, at most 10 MiB. Pass native IHP main/maximal DRC without waivers (standalone scope; density/antenna disabled), strict named-interface LVS with explicit taps and a 3300 × 140 um functional envelope. All functional device, contact and routing drawing layers listed in the runtime outline constraint contribute to bounding-box area; annotation and pin-purpose layers do not.

Post-layout simulation uses the candidate's Magic RC netlist, including physical MIM/poly devices and interconnect parasitics, with explicit handling of half-grid GDS import. Magic idealizes substrate/well contacts; source simulation retains finite contact models. Distributed substrate resistance, substrate noise and manufacturing signoff are outside scope.
sections.Tools and Submission:
Solve budget: 3 hours.

Discover inputs, resources and feedback through /protocol/task.json, /protocol/resources.json and /protocol/harness.json. Use the provided IHP primitives and KLayout, Magic and ngspice. Write /workspace/output/final.gds, then submit explicitly through the runtime protocol. Host configuration, source records and reference layouts are not standard solver inputs.

/api/task-guides/ihp-sg13g2.analog-db.am.title: Current-Buffered Compensation OTA

/api/task-guides/ihp-sg13g2.analog-db.am.description_html:
Output-Controlled Auxiliary Compensation OTA Layout Task

Objective

Lay out amp_006_leung_dfcfc1, retaining the complete folded PMOS-input stage, three-stage signal path, direct output feedforward, and auxiliary compensation. The folded stage drives net050, which drives the output PMOS and the PMOS/diode/mirror path to net049. That node drives both the output NMOS and an auxiliary common-source NMOS whose drain is net1; a biased PMOS loads this auxiliary drain. C0 connects net050 to output, while C1 connects net049 to net1. The auxiliary branch therefore acts on the NMOS output control node. In contrast, the separate AMP007 case's auxiliary PMOS senses net050 and its compensation terminates at net2.

Inputs and Interface

  • materials/circuit.cdl: authoritative native physical device graph.
  • materials/circuit.spice: matching simulator representation with logical body nets.
  • materials/testbench.spice: public bias, bilateral AC and step measurements.

Ordered ports: vss vdd vinn vinp vout net013. VSS is return, VDD supply, VINN/VINP the inverting/noninverting inputs, VOUT output, and net013 the external bias-sink connection. Input PMOS bodies connect to the separate net31 source-tied well; other PMOS use the VDD well and NMOS use the VSS substrate. Preserve all 26 MOS groups, W/L/m, body connections, and both internal capacitive branches. Native equivalent parallel fingering is allowed only when all physical and electrical checks pass.

MOS dimensions retain the declared grid adaptation. All capacitors are physical cap_cmim:

  • c0: net050 (top plate) to vout (bottom plate), 8 parallel 48.935 × 48.935 um MIM units.
  • c1: net049 (top plate) to net1 (bottom plate), 3 parallel 50.94 × 50.94 um MIM units.

These are internal compensation devices, distinct from the external load. The normalized source's 27.4754 uA bias is deliberately calibrated to 6.86885 uA, improving headroom and finite tracking at the declared signal levels. No ideal output servo or internal numerical damping element is added.

Operating Conditions

Use typical IHP LV MOS/MIM/poly models at 27 C and VDD=1.2 V, with an external 6.86885 uA sink from net013 to VSS. Every combination of 5/10/20 pF output load and 0.5/0.7 V DC input must pass. A zero-volt source from VINN (vm) to VOUT closes unity feedback. VINP is AC ground. The two DC input levels independently check operating-point error and the complete sampled return ratio.

At the closed input/output boundary, inject a series AC voltage with zero parallel AC current, then zero series voltage and unit current into vm. Both injections retain the original circuit and loading. With first-run b=-I(VPROBE), d=V(vm) and second-run a=-I(VPROBE), c=V(vm), define delta=a*d-b*c and the bilateral return ratio T=(2*delta-a+d)/(1-2*delta+a-d) (Tian et al., Eq. 30). The deck exports both injections' voltages/currents for independent two-port admittance reconstruction. This is a finite external-loop measurement, not a certificate for every internal pole or a complete Nyquist proof.

Sweep 0.01 Hz–10 GHz at 300 points/decade. Use continuous phase starting on its natural low-frequency branch, without a phase-offset correction. Check both first and final descending unity crossings, minimum sampled abs(1+T), maximum absolute continuous phase of 1+T across the entire sweep, and maximum gain over 2–10 GHz. Missing crossings or invalid measurements are evaluator errors; both first and final phase margins must lie in [0, 180] degrees. Minimum return distance and return-phase excursion have only nonnegative domain bounds; high-frequency gain has no acceptance bound. These full-sweep observations affect continuous quality and do not establish a stability certificate.

For each condition, VINP's pulse starts at 0.5 V, rises to 0.7 V at 2–2.02 us and falls at 10.02–10.04 us, with a 16 us period. Transient uses its own pulse-start operating point, independently of the AC DC-input setting. Simulate 0–18 us with the KLU linear solver and Gear order 2, 2 ns maximum step, itl4=1000, rshunt=1e12, reltol=1e-5, abstol=1e-12, and vntol=1e-8. The numerical shunt is not a physical device. The maintained 1 pA absolute current tolerance is checked at 0.1 pA with tenfold tighter relative/voltage tolerances and a 1e13 ohm shunt. Initial experimental 10 fA/1 fA current tolerances produced excessive iteration cost in the extracted low-resistance network. This numerical-floor calibration preserves every electrical bound and all physical/parasitic elements; half-step and trapezoidal controls independently check the observable dynamics. PVT, mismatch, noise, distortion, supply startup, rail-to-rail operation and arbitrary-load stability are outside this contract.

Physical Requirements

Submit GDSII top cell amp_006_leung_dfcfc1, at most 32 MiB. Pass native IHP main/maximal DRC without waivers (standalone scope, density/antenna off), strict named-interface LVS with physically verified body connections, and a 6400 × 130 um functional envelope. Every device/contact/interconnect drawing layer listed in the runtime outline constraint contributes to area; annotation/pin-purpose layers do not. Labels alone do not establish electrical connectivity.

Post-layout simulation uses the submitted GDS's complete Magic RC, with physical MIM devices and interconnect resistances/capacitances. Half-grid import is explicit. Magic retains only Metal3 interface labels in its isolated extraction copy to avoid repeated internal well-name aliases, while native LVS checks the original GDS and its actual body-contact connectivity. No resistance/capacitance threshold omits small parasitics. Source simulation and extraction use the same logical body-net boundary. Distributed substrate resistance/noise and fabrication signoff remain unqualified. The long independent witness is a feasibility layout, not an area optimum.

Electrical Requirements and Scoring

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Quality scoring imposes no fixed degradation allowance. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. Independent source observations remain required evidence. The explicit quality targets below supply scoring anchors; otherwise the paired source value is used. Reports retain every paired result.

Let x be the post-layout measurement and b the declared quality target, or the same-condition source measurement when no target is declared:

  • Ratio normalization: maximize with q = x/b and minimize with q = b/x. When a numerical scale s is declared, use (x+s)/(b+s) and its reciprocal, respectively. The scale handles zero values as a normalization floor; it is neither an allowed degradation nor an acceptance bound.
  • Amplitude in dB: maximize with q = 10^((x-b)/20) and minimize with its reciprocal.
  • Target normalization: q = 1/(1+abs(x-b)/s), where s is the declared physical scale. Signed or zero-valued operating points are not divided directly.

Use layout scoring. First compute each metric's raw quality q from the worst paired condition, with raw area quality q_area = area_target / candidate_functional_area. Credit c_i = min(1, q_i) for every positively weighted metric, then compute S = 100 * product(c_i ** w_i). The weights sum to 1 and the score is bounded by 100. An improvement beyond one target cannot compensate for missing another target. Physical or functional rejection scores zero; missing or invalid measurements leave the score unknown, and zero-weight observations must also be valid. Reaching every positively weighted target scores 100; a feasible reference may score far below 100. Weights express quality tradeoffs, not acceptance bounds.

The measurements below use the supplied SPICE node and source names. v(n) is a node voltage; i(V) is current flowing into a voltage source, so delivered power uses a negative sign. db(z)=20*log10(abs(z)); mag/abs denote magnitude, and cph denotes continuous phase in radians. find, when, from/to and rise/fall follow the deck's interpolation, window and crossing conventions. SPICE suffixes p/n/u/m/meg/g mean pico/nano/micro/milli/mega/giga. Nested avg, min, max, vecmin/vecmax and deriv represent window averages, extrema and sampled derivatives. Measure each operating condition independently, pair it with the source result under that condition, and take the worst paired quality within each metric group.

For metrics declaring saturating_ratio, q = 2(b+s)/(b+x+2*s), using the quality anchor b and the positive scale s in the metric’s units. Equality to the anchor gives raw quality 1; improvements approach raw quality 2 but credited quality stays at 1. Normalize each condition before selecting the worst quality. These scales and targets do not add acceptance cutoffs.

output_error_v DC operating point: abs(v(vout)-v(vp)). V minimize / saturating_ratio 0 … +∞ 2e-06 bias

unity_hz AC: Crossing coordinate where (db((T)))=0 fall=1. Hz maximize / ratio 0 … +∞ — response

final_unity_hz AC: Crossing coordinate where (db((T)))=0 fall=last. Hz maximize / ratio 0 … +∞ — response
final_phase_margin_deg AC: 180+(find (180*cph((T))/pi) when (db((T)))=0 fall=last). deg target / target 0 … 180 180 response
minimum_return_distance AC: vecmin((mag(1+(T)))); sweep dec 300 0.01 10g. 1 maximize / ratio 0 … +∞ 1e-12 response
return_phase_excursion_deg AC: vecmax(abs(180*cph(1+(T))/pi)); sweep dec 300 0.01 10g. deg minimize / ratio 0 … +∞ 1e-12 response
hf_gain_db AC: Maximum of (db((T))) from=2g to=10g. dB minimize / db20 −∞ … +∞ — response
recovery_up_v TRAN: Maximum of (abs(v(vout)-v(vp))) from=5u to=9.5u. V minimize / saturating_ratio 0 … +∞ 1e-06 response
recovery_down_v TRAN: Maximum of (abs(v(vout)-v(vp))) from=13u to=17.5u. V minimize / saturating_ratio 0 … +∞ 1e-06 response

peak_v TRAN: Maximum of v(vout) from=2u to=10u. V target / target 0 … 1.2 1.2 response
trough_v TRAN: Minimum of v(vout) from=10.04u to=18u. V target / target 0 … 1.2 1.2 response

Area reference: 82915.92 um2. The reference engineering estimate used 1164 device instances, a sum of device/contact envelopes 54901.4182 um2, a one-sided envelope margin of 0.6 um, a routing allowance of 50%, and a total outer width/height allowance 1.2 um. Estimate = ceil(100 * (1.5 * envelope_sum + 2 * margin * sqrt(envelope_sum) + margin^2)) / 100. Here margin is the total allowance across both sides, and the envelope sum is displayed to four decimal places. Reference MOS/passive envelopes use W/L (or resistor dimensions) and multiplicity, including explicit contacts and HBT emitter/contact envelopes. This is a frozen engineering estimate, not a process minimum or a proven achievable area.

The capability coefficient is 8, independent of this task's reference-normalized score.

Quality targets and weights

The area quality target is 34000 um2. It is an integration budget, not a hard limit or a proven process minimum.

The eleven fixed MIM plates occupy 26941.7246 um2. A 34000 um2 integration budget allocates about 79% to those plates and the balance to enclosures, 675 MOS fingers, taps and routing; it is not a process minimum. Area carries 30%, 100 ppm step-referred DC accuracy 15%, the worst bilateral normalized response integral 20%, bandwidth 10%, phase-margin preservation 10%, sampled return distance 5%, large-signal step gain 5% and mean power 5%. First/final crossing diagnostics and fully settled recovery errors are retained without duplicate weight. Source and extraction use the same logical body-net boundary.

response_time_s takes the worst of both normalized absolute-error integrals under every declared condition: integrate abs(v(vout)-high_v)/0.2 over 2.02–9.5 us, and abs(v(vout)-low_v)/0.2 over 10.04–17.5 us. high_v and low_v are the existing late-window means. The result is in seconds; a first-order exponential would integrate to its time constant over a sufficiently long window. The 500 ns budget leaves about 6 ns above the worst 494 ns source result. This finite-window response cost is not a measured settling time or a guarantee of later convergence. DC offset and large-signal step gain are scored separately, preventing a flat or wrong-amplitude response from satisfying all goals.

functional_area 34000 um2 — 0.3
output_error_v 2e-05 V 2e-06 0.15
minimum_return_distance 0.9 1 1e-12 0.05
phase_margin_deg paired source deg 10 0.1
unity_hz paired source Hz — 0.1
step_gain 1 V/V 0.01 0.05
mean_power_w paired source W 1e-12 0.05
response_time_s 5e-07 s 1e-09 0.2

Zero-weight observations: recovery_down_v, recovery_up_v, final_phase_margin_deg, return_phase_excursion_deg, dc_gain_db, final_unity_hz, hf_gain_db, peak_v, trough_v, bias_v, output_v, power_w. Original functional requirements remain enforced; grouped metrics listed above carry their stated weight once.

The targets affect continuous quality only. A complete feasible reference may miss them; there is no minimum qualifying score.

Tools and Submission

Solve budget: 1.5 hours.

Discover inputs/resources/feedback through /protocol/task.json, /protocol/resources.json and /protocol/harness.json. Use the supplied IHP primitives with KLayout, Magic and ngspice. Write /workspace/output/final.gds and explicitly submit via the harness protocol. Host configuration, source records and reference answers are outside solver inputs.

The authoritative MOS input preserves the original logical groups, W/L/m and all four terminal nets. Verified unit arrays, multiple fingers, shared diffusion and shared wells on the same body net are allowed. Native LVS checks connectivity and equivalent device parameters; native DRC checks actual well/substrate contacts. Contact count, dimensions, area/perimeter and the reference well partition are not circuit constraints. PEX uses actual diffusion geometry and interconnect RC, with logical body nets as its boundary; distributed substrate/well resistance is outside this extraction model.

Ordered ports: vss vdd vinn vinp vout net013. VSS is return, VDD supply, VINN/VINP the inverting/noninverting inputs, VOUT output, and net013 the external bias-sink connection. Input PMOS bodies connect to the separate net31 source-tied well; other PMOS use the VDD well and NMOS use the VSS substrate. Preserve all 26 MOS groups, W/L/m, body connections, and both internal capacitive branches. Native equivalent parallel fingering is allowed only when all physical and electrical checks pass.

MOS dimensions retain the declared grid adaptation. All capacitors are physical cap_cmim:

  • c0: net050 (top plate) to vout (bottom plate), 8 parallel 48.935 × 48.935 um MIM units.
  • c1: net049 (top plate) to net1 (bottom plate), 3 parallel 50.94 × 50.94 um MIM units.

These are internal compensation devices, distinct from the external load. The normalized source's 27.4754 uA bias is deliberately calibrated to 6.86885 uA, improving headroom and finite tracking at the declared signal levels. No ideal output servo or internal numerical damping element is added.
sections.Objective: Lay out amp_006_leung_dfcfc1, retaining the complete folded PMOS-input stage, three-stage signal path, direct output feedforward, and auxiliary compensation. The folded stage drives net050, which drives the output PMOS and the PMOS/diode/mirror path to net049. That node drives both the output NMOS and an auxiliary common-source NMOS whose drain is net1; a biased PMOS loads this auxiliary drain. C0 connects net050 to output, while C1 connects net049 to net1. The auxiliary branch therefore acts on the NMOS output control node. In contrast, the separate AMP007 case's auxiliary PMOS senses net050 and its compensation terminates at net2.
sections.Operating Conditions:
Use typical IHP LV MOS/MIM/poly models at 27 C and VDD=1.2 V, with an external 6.86885 uA sink from net013 to VSS. Every combination of 5/10/20 pF output load and 0.5/0.7 V DC input must pass. A zero-volt source from VINN (vm) to VOUT closes unity feedback. VINP is AC ground. The two DC input levels independently check operating-point error and the complete sampled return ratio.

At the closed input/output boundary, inject a series AC voltage with zero parallel AC current, then zero series voltage and unit current into vm. Both injections retain the original circuit and loading. With first-run b=-I(VPROBE), d=V(vm) and second-run a=-I(VPROBE), c=V(vm), define delta=a*d-b*c and the bilateral return ratio T=(2*delta-a+d)/(1-2*delta+a-d) (Tian et al., Eq. 30). The deck exports both injections' voltages/currents for independent two-port admittance reconstruction. This is a finite external-loop measurement, not a certificate for every internal pole or a complete Nyquist proof.

Sweep 0.01 Hz–10 GHz at 300 points/decade. Use continuous phase starting on its natural low-frequency branch, without a phase-offset correction. Check both first and final descending unity crossings, minimum sampled abs(1+T), maximum absolute continuous phase of 1+T across the entire sweep, and maximum gain over 2–10 GHz. Missing crossings or invalid measurements are evaluator errors; both first and final phase margins must lie in [0, 180] degrees. Minimum return distance and return-phase excursion have only nonnegative domain bounds; high-frequency gain has no acceptance bound. These full-sweep observations affect continuous quality and do not establish a stability certificate.

For each condition, VINP's pulse starts at 0.5 V, rises to 0.7 V at 2–2.02 us and falls at 10.02–10.04 us, with a 16 us period. Transient uses its own pulse-start operating point, independently of the AC DC-input setting. Simulate 0–18 us with the KLU linear solver and Gear order 2, 2 ns maximum step, itl4=1000, rshunt=1e12, reltol=1e-5, abstol=1e-12, and vntol=1e-8. The numerical shunt is not a physical device. The maintained 1 pA absolute current tolerance is checked at 0.1 pA with tenfold tighter relative/voltage tolerances and a 1e13 ohm shunt. Initial experimental 10 fA/1 fA current tolerances produced excessive iteration cost in the extracted low-resistance network. This numerical-floor calibration preserves every electrical bound and all physical/parasitic elements; half-step and trapezoidal controls independently check the observable dynamics. PVT, mismatch, noise, distortion, supply startup, rail-to-rail operation and arbitrary-load stability are outside this contract.
sections.Physical Requirements:
Submit GDSII top cell amp_006_leung_dfcfc1, at most 32 MiB. Pass native IHP main/maximal DRC without waivers (standalone scope, density/antenna off), strict named-interface LVS with physically verified body connections, and a 6400 × 130 um functional envelope. Every device/contact/interconnect drawing layer listed in the runtime outline constraint contributes to area; annotation/pin-purpose layers do not. Labels alone do not establish electrical connectivity.

Post-layout simulation uses the submitted GDS's complete Magic RC, with physical MIM devices and interconnect resistances/capacitances. Half-grid import is explicit. Magic retains only Metal3 interface labels in its isolated extraction copy to avoid repeated internal well-name aliases, while native LVS checks the original GDS and its actual body-contact connectivity. No resistance/capacitance threshold omits small parasitics. Source simulation and extraction use the same logical body-net boundary. Distributed substrate resistance/noise and fabrication signoff remain unqualified. The long independent witness is a feasibility layout, not an area optimum.
sections.Tools and Submission:
Solve budget: 1.5 hours.

Discover inputs/resources/feedback through /protocol/task.json, /protocol/resources.json and /protocol/harness.json. Use the supplied IHP primitives with KLayout, Magic and ngspice. Write /workspace/output/final.gds and explicitly submit via the harness protocol. Host configuration, source records and reference answers are outside solver inputs.

The authoritative MOS input preserves the original logical groups, W/L/m and all four terminal nets. Verified unit arrays, multiple fingers, shared diffusion and shared wells on the same body net are allowed. Native LVS checks connectivity and equivalent device parameters; native DRC checks actual well/substrate contacts. Contact count, dimensions, area/perimeter and the reference well partition are not circuit constraints. PEX uses actual diffusion geometry and interconnect RC, with logical body nets as its boundary; distributed substrate/well resistance is outside this extraction model.

/api/task-guides/ihp-sg13g2.analog-db.am.description_html:
Auxiliary-Stage Miller Compensation OTA Layout Task

Objective

Lay out amp_007_leung_dfcfc2 with its physical compensation and fixed transistor network, for the declared loop response and sustained unity-feedback step recovery.

The folded PMOS-input stage drives net050; the PMOS/diode/mirror path drives net049 and then the NMOS output stage. Direct feedforward drives the output PMOS from net050. A separate PMOS common-source branch has gate net050, drain net2 and an NMOS bias sink. C1 connects net050 to output; C2 connects net050 to net2, across the auxiliary stage. This compensation branch is distinct from output-to-current-buffer injection and from the net049-controlled auxiliary termination in the other cases.

The maintained circuit retains all 26 source MOS groups as 440 physical fingers, 10 MIM units and 0 high-poly segments. All MOS dimensions/multiplicities are retained exactly. The maintained 20 uA sink is external through net1. The source bias-current value is retained. Physical substrate and separate N-well contacts retain the input PMOS bodies at their common source net31, electrically separate from the VDD well. No internal ideal bias source or output servo is introduced. Capacitor values are rounded to physical geometry; every branch remains internal to the DUT.

Inputs and Interface

  • materials/circuit.cdl: authoritative native LVS circuit.
  • materials/circuit.spice: simulation circuit bound to the process models.
  • materials/testbench.spice: bias, AC injection and transient tests.

Ordered ports: vss vdd vinn vinp vout net1. VSS is return, VDD is supply, VINN/VINP are inverting/noninverting inputs, VOUT is output, and net1 connects the external 20 uA sink to VSS. Input PMOS bodies retain the separate source-tied well; other PMOS bodies use the VDD well and NMOS bodies use the VSS substrate contact. Preserve device W/L/m, body connectivity, all internal branches and total multiplicities in the authoritative netlist. Native equivalent parallel fingers are allowed only when LVS and electrical requirements pass. Do not short distinct ports or create extra driven monitors.

Internal passive devices are listed below; external loads are declared separately:

  • c1: net050 → vout, 5 parallel cap_cmim unit(s), each 47.61 × 47.61 um; nominal total 17.038429 pF.
  • c2: net050 → net2, 5 parallel cap_cmim unit(s), each 47.61 × 47.61 um; nominal total 17.038429 pF.

Operating Conditions

Use typical MOS/MIM/poly models at 27 C, VDD=1.2 V and the declared external bias. All three output loads, 5/10/20 pF, must pass. At DC, VINP=0.5 V and VOUT feeds back to VINN through a zero-volt measurement source. For AC, inject 1 V in series with the feedback connection and set VINP AC=0; the return ratio at the high-impedance MOS input boundary is T=-V(vout)/V(vm). Sweep 150 points per decade from 0.01 Hz to 100 MHz with continuous phase, without arbitrary correction of the low-frequency phase offset. The first falling 0 dB crossing defines unity-gain frequency, and 180+phase(T) at that crossing defines phase margin. A missing crossing is an evaluation error.

VINP rises from 0.5 V to 0.7 V during 2–2.02 us and falls during 10.02–10.04 us, repeating every 16 us. Simulate 0–18 us with second-order Gear, a maximum step of 2 ns, rshunt=1e12, reltol=1e-5, abstol=1e-14 and vntol=1e-8. Numerical shunt branches are not physical bias or startup devices. PVT, mismatch, noise, distortion, rail-to-rail operation, power-up and stability under arbitrary loads are outside scope.

The transient nonlinear iteration ceiling is explicitly itl4=1000, with unchanged accuracy tolerances. This allows the retained high-multiplicity mirror/auxiliary network to converge; it is not a relaxed acceptance limit.

Physical Requirements

Submit GDSII top cell amp_007_leung_dfcfc2, at most 10 MiB. Pass native IHP main/maximal DRC without waivers (standalone scope; density/antenna disabled), strict named-interface LVS with explicit taps and a 3500 × 130 um functional envelope. All functional device, contact and routing drawing layers listed in the runtime outline constraint contribute to bounding-box area; annotation and pin-purpose layers do not.

Post-layout simulation uses the candidate's Magic RC netlist, including physical MIM/poly devices and interconnect parasitics, with explicit handling of half-grid GDS import. Magic idealizes substrate/well contacts; source simulation retains finite contact models. Distributed substrate resistance, substrate noise and manufacturing signoff are outside scope.

Electrical Requirements and Scoring

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Quality scoring imposes no fixed degradation allowance. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. Independent source observations define the 100-point electrical baseline without depending on the submitted GDS; reports retain every paired result.

Let x be the post-layout measurement and b the source-circuit measurement under the same conditions:

  • Ratio normalization: maximize with q = x/b and minimize with q = b/x. When a numerical scale s is declared, use (x+s)/(b+s) and its reciprocal, respectively. The scale handles zero values as a normalization floor; it is neither an allowed degradation nor an acceptance bound.
  • Amplitude in dB: maximize with q = 10^((x-b)/20) and minimize with its reciprocal.
  • Target normalization: q = 1/(1+abs(x-b)/s), where s is the declared physical scale. Signed or zero-valued operating points are not divided directly.

Use layout scoring. Each metric takes its worst paired quality q, and the total score is S = 100 * product(q_i ** w_i), with area quality q_area = area_reference / candidate_functional_area. The weights below sum to 1; metric dimensions describe measurements and do not determine weights. Physical or functional rejection scores zero; missing or invalid measurements leave the score unknown, and zero-weight observations must also be valid. Matching source-circuit performance at the reference area scores 100 points; better valid solutions may exceed 100. Weights express quality tradeoffs rather than hard bounds.

The measurements below use the supplied SPICE node and source names. v(n) is a node voltage; i(V) is current flowing into a voltage source, so delivered power uses a negative sign. db(z)=20*log10(abs(z)); mag/abs denote magnitude, and cph denotes continuous phase in radians. find, when, from/to and rise/fall follow the deck's interpolation, window and crossing conventions. SPICE suffixes p/n/u/m/meg/g mean pico/nano/micro/milli/mega/giga. Nested avg, min, max, vecmin/vecmax and deriv represent window averages, extrema and sampled derivatives. Measure each operating condition independently, pair it with the source result under that condition, and take the worst paired quality within each metric group.

recovery_up_v and recovery_down_v use saturating_ratio. Candidate error x, paired source error b and the positive scale s below define q = 2(b+s)/(b+x+2s). Source-equivalent error gives q=1; decreasing error approaches the upper quality limit 2 with diminishing returns. The scale retains its declared unit and numerical-floor meaning. Normalize each operating condition before taking the worst paired quality; other metrics retain their own declared normalization and functional requirements.

trough_v TRAN: Minimum of v(vout) from=10.04u to=18u. V target / target 0 … 1.2 1.2 response

Area reference: 52764.97 um2. The expanded circuit has 453 device instances, a sum of device/contact envelopes 34876.8788 um2, a one-sided envelope margin of 0.6 um, a routing allowance of 50%, and a total outer width/height allowance 1.2 um. Estimate = ceil(100 * (1.5 * envelope_sum + 2 * margin * sqrt(envelope_sum) + margin^2)) / 100. Here margin is the total allowance across both sides, and the envelope sum is displayed to four decimal places. MOS/passive envelopes use W/L (or resistor dimensions) and multiplicity, including explicit contacts and HBT emitter/contact envelopes. This is a frozen engineering estimate, not a process minimum or a proven achievable area.

The capability coefficient is 8, independent of this task's reference-normalized score.

Compensated feedback amplifiers: loaded recovery 28.6%, loop margin 20.5%, gain and bandwidth 16.4%, step transfer and extrema 8.18%, bias 4.09%, power 12.3%, area 10%. Each objective's weight is divided equally among its metrics.

Dual-Capacitor Three-Stage OTA Layout Task

sections.Objective:
Lay out amp_010_peng_acbc with its physical compensation and fixed transistor network, for the declared loop response and sustained unity-feedback step recovery.

The folded PMOS-input stage drives net050; a PMOS/diode/mirror stage drives net049, followed by the NMOS output stage. The output PMOS also receives feedforward drive from net050. C0 connects net050 to output, while C1 connects net049 to net1. The auxiliary node has a bias-fed PMOS, a diode-connected PMOS and an NMOS controlled by net043; this three-device branch creates a distinct active compensation termination. It is neither a second output-connected Miller capacitor nor the six-MOS current-buffer branch of the other representative.

The maintained circuit retains all 27 source MOS groups as 237 physical fingers, 6 MIM units and 0 high-poly segments. MOS W/L are rounded to the nearest 0.01 um process grid. All source multiplicities are retained. The maintained 1.80825 uA sink is external through net013. The external bias is deliberately calibrated to 0.1 times the source current; this is not an unchanged upstream operating point. Physical substrate and separate N-well contacts retain the input PMOS bodies at their common source net31, electrically separate from the VDD well. No internal ideal bias source or output servo is introduced. Capacitor values are rounded to physical geometry; every branch remains internal to the DUT.

/api/task-guides/ihp-sg13g2.analog-db.am.description_html:
Peng IAC Three-Stage Amplifier Layout Task

Objective

Implement amp_011_peng_iac with the supplied fixed topology and dimensions. The PMOS input pair and cascoded branches feed voutn/voutp. The PMOS bias mirror is cascoded with vb2, generated by XM65/XM63/XM64. XM10 drives net043; XM67/XM68 and XM70 retain the auxiliary current path, with XM69 driving net10 against XM66. XM11/XM23 drive vout. Compensation retains 1.95593 pF between voutp and vout, and 4.33595 pF between net10 and net4 with 1.46466 Mohm from net4 to vss. Do not replace the circuit, delete compensation, or add a servo. The physical core contains 34 logical MOS groups with upstream multiplicities. Each PMOS input body remains tied to its own tail node through its physical well contact.

Inputs and Interface

materials/circuit.cdl is the physical authority; materials/circuit.spice is its matching simulator representation. materials/testbench.spice defines closed-loop observations and materials/ac.spice defines balanced differential AC excitation. Ordered ports: vss vdd vinn vinp vout vb1. vss is ground, vdd supply, vinn/vinp negative/positive input, vout the single-ended output, and vb1 the external bias-current sink. Bias, input drivers, feedback wiring and load are external test apparatus; all internal R/C and actual body contacts are physical DUT elements.

Operating Conditions

IHP SG13G2, nominal TT/typical, 27 C, supply 1.5 V, input reference 0.24 V, external current sink 7.11568e-07 A to vss, and 10 pF output load. Use the fixed IHP LV binding at 1.5 V, adapting the authored 1.8 V stimulus to the LV process rail; retain its bias current and input reference. Round W/L to 10 nm so half-gate contacts remain on grid. The closed-loop deck ties vinn directly to vout, drives vinp with a +100 mV pulse starting at 2 us (100 ns rise/fall, 18 us high duration), and runs to 40 us with 2 ns maximum steps, Gear order 2, reltol=1e-5, abstol=1 pA, vntol=10 nV. A disconnected timing marker forces exact integration-window endpoints. Transient starts from the solved DC point; this is not a zero-state supply-ramp startup test. High and return windows are 15–20 and 35–40 us.

AC spans 1 Hz–1 GHz at 200 points/decade. The differential deck retains DC output feedback through a 1 GH inductor and AC-isolates its bias node with 1 kF to ground; vinp/vinn receive balanced +0.5/-0.5 V small-signal excitation. It verifies residual input common-mode amplitude <=1 uV and DC feedback mismatch <=1 uV. These are external small-signal bias fixtures, not physical compensation. Both decks use rshunt=1e12 ohm to regularize otherwise floating extracted nodes; this numerical conductance is applied equally to source and candidate and is not a DUT compensation branch. The separate closed-loop deck measures actual follower response. No voltage-transfer estimate is labeled a loop return ratio.

Physical Requirements

Supply a GDS <=64 MiB with top cell amp_011_peng_iac, within 20000 by 2000 um (the task's artifact-size/outline bounds). Native DRC, strict named-interface LVS and functional-area measurement must pass; no marker waivers apply. Preserve MOS dimensions, multiplicities, body connections, all physical R/C and logical body connectivity. Functional layers in the published task include active, implant, wells, gates, contacts, passive plates, vias and routing; annotation/text-only layers are excluded. IHP native main and maximal DRC use the pinned PDK block profiles, with chip-level density and antenna disabled. Native MIM and high-poly primitives retain their compact models. Magic idealizes well/substrate taps; source simulation uses the declared logical body connections. This is not distributed substrate or RF/EM extraction. Candidate-derived Magic distributed RC feeds every post-layout job.

Electrical Requirements and Scoring

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Quality scoring imposes no fixed degradation allowance. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. Independent source observations define the 100-point electrical baseline without depending on the submitted GDS; reports retain every paired result.

Let x be the post-layout measurement and b the source-circuit measurement under the same conditions:

  • Ratio normalization: maximize with q = x/b and minimize with q = b/x. When a numerical scale s is declared, use (x+s)/(b+s) and its reciprocal, respectively. The scale handles zero values as a normalization floor; it is neither an allowed degradation nor an acceptance bound.
  • Amplitude in dB: maximize with q = 10^((x-b)/20) and minimize with its reciprocal.
  • Target normalization: q = 1/(1+abs(x-b)/s), where s is the declared physical scale. Signed or zero-valued operating points are not divided directly.

Use layout scoring. Each metric takes its worst paired quality q, and the total score is S = 100 * product(q_i ** w_i), with area quality q_area = area_reference / candidate_functional_area. The weights below sum to 1; metric dimensions describe measurements and do not determine weights. Physical or functional rejection scores zero; missing or invalid measurements leave the score unknown, and zero-weight observations must also be valid. Matching source-circuit performance at the reference area scores 100 points; better valid solutions may exceed 100. Weights express quality tradeoffs rather than hard bounds.

late_error_v, return_error_v, ripple_v and return_ripple_v use saturating_ratio. Candidate error x, paired source error b and the positive scale s below define q = 2(b+s)/(b+x+2s). Source-equivalent error gives q=1; decreasing error approaches the upper quality limit 2 with diminishing returns. The scale retains its declared unit and numerical-floor meaning. Normalize each condition before taking the worst paired quality; other metrics retain their declared normalization and functional requirements.

All measurements must be finite and complete. Supply power, absolute errors and amplitude ranges must obey their nonnegative physical definitions. The common-mode test-apparatus bound validates differential excitation, rather than DUT common-mode regulation. The DC feedback bound excludes failure of the isolated bias solve. Both apparatus checks apply to source and candidate simulation before scoring. These are this task's hard electrical requirements; upstream paper targets are not acceptance bounds. Window error and ripple do not establish settling or periodic steady state; no phase margin, unity-gain crossing, settling time, CMRR, noise, PVT or mismatch performance is claimed.

Quality uses independently simulated same-condition source observations. For gain, q=10^((candidate−source)/20); target q=1/(1+abs(candidate−source)/scale); inverse-ratio q=(source+floor)/(candidate+floor). The 6 dB target scale corresponds to a factor-of-two amplitude change; 1.5 V is the bias normalization and 1 mV is 1% of the 100 mV test step, preventing numerical zero error from dominating quality. This is an engineering estimate, not a foundry minimum. Coefficient 8: Active auxiliary current feedback, cascoded bias, and two interacting compensation paths affect finite-window recovery and frequency response.

Score weights

Finite-window amplifier response: tracking error 36%, ripple 22.5%, AC transfer 18%, bias and offset 4.5%, power 9%, area 10%. Each objective's weight is divided equally among its metrics.

/api/task-guides/ihp-sg13g2.analog-db.am.title: Peng IAC Three-Stage Amplifier

/api/task-guides/ihp-sg13g2.analog-db.am.description_html:
Auxiliary Source-Driven Output-Control OTA Layout Task

Objective

Lay out amp_012_peng_tcfc with its complete transistor signal and bias paths. The PMOS-input folded stage produces voutp, driving the output PMOS and net043 branch. The large PMOS path through net049 feeds net10, while net043 controls its NMOS pulldown. net10 drives the output NMOS. Preserve both original compensation branches and the added local output-control MIM. Unlike a direct net050/net049 output stage, this circuit includes the source-driven auxiliary PMOS and a separate net10 control node.

Inputs and Interface

  • materials/circuit.cdl: authoritative native physical connectivity.
  • materials/circuit.spice: equivalent simulation connectivity with logical body nets.
  • materials/testbench.spice: DC, bilateral-loop and sustained-step measurements.

Ordered ports: vss vdd vinn vinp vout vb1. VSS/VDD are return/supply; VINN/VINP are inverting/noninverting inputs; VOUT is output; vb1 connects to the external bias sink. Input PMOS bodies use the separate net31 source-tied well; other PMOS use VDD and NMOS use the VSS substrate. Preserve all 32 MOS groups, W/L/m, every body connection and all physical passive devices.

MOS dimensions retain the declared grid adaptation. All internal capacitors use cap_cmim:

  • c0: voutp (top) to vout (bottom), 1 parallel 35.325 × 35.325 um MIM units.
  • c1: net049 (top) to vout (bottom), 1 parallel 41.2 × 41.2 um MIM units.
  • clocal: net10 (top) to vout (bottom), 1 parallel 51.64 × 51.64 um MIM units.

The raw 1.29849 uA sink is calibrated to 0.16231125 uA. A real approximately 4 pF net10–vout MIM is added to suppress the internal output-control oscillation. Both original 1.87196 pF voutp–vout and 2.54606 pF net049–vout branches remain. There is no added output-to-ground capacitor. No ideal servo, diagnostic clamp or hidden damping element is part of this DUT.

Operating Conditions

Use typical IHP LV MOS/MIM/poly models at 27 C and VDD=1.2 V, with a 0.162311 uA sink from vb1 to VSS. All combinations of external 5/10/15 pF load and 0.5/0.7 V DC input must pass. These external loads are additional to every internal capacitor above.

A zero-volt source connects VINN (vm) to VOUT, while VINP is AC ground. Insert series voltage injection and parallel current injection at this boundary, retaining the complete DUT and load. Voltage injection uses b=-I(VPROBE), d=V(vm); current injection uses a=-I(VPROBE), c=V(vm); delta=a*d-b*c, T=(2*delta-a+d)/(1-2*delta+a-d) (Tian expression 30). Export both raw injections to independently reconstruct the Y matrix. Sweep 300 points per decade from 0.01 Hz to 10 GHz; continuous phase follows the natural low-frequency branch without offset correction. Check first and last descending unity-gain crossings, full-sweep minimum sampled abs(1+T), maximum absolute continuous phase over 1+T, and gain over 2–10 GHz; a good first crossing alone is insufficient.

VINP is a 0.5→0.7→0.5 V pulse with 20 ns edges, rising at 2 us and falling at 20.02 us with period 100 us. Transient starts at its own initial-pulse operating point, independently of the AC DC-input setting. Simulate 0–40 us with Gear2, maximum step 2 ns, KLU, itl4=1000, rshunt=1e12, reltol=1e-5, abstol=1e-12, vntol=1e-8; numerical shunts are not physical devices. Verification also covers half steps, tighter tolerances/denser AC, trapezoidal integration, long tails and finite excitation/load boundaries. These finite outer-loop and recovery observations do not prove internal poles, stability under arbitrary loads, PVT, noise, mismatch, distortion, rail-to-rail operation or power-up startup performance.

The phase margins at the first and last crossings must both lie within [0, 180] degrees. Minimum return distance and return-phase excursion need only be nonnegative; high-frequency gain has no acceptance threshold. These full-sweep metrics affect continuous quality without adding stability acceptance conditions. Missing crossings or invalid observations are evaluation errors.

Physical Requirements

Submit GDSII top cell amp_012_peng_tcfc, at most 32 MiB. Native IHP main/maximal DRC must pass without waivers (standalone scope, density/antenna off), together with strict named-interface LVS and a 1400 × 160 um functional envelope. All device/contact/interconnect drawing layers in the runtime outline constraint contribute to area; annotation/pin-purpose layers do not. Post-layout simulation uses the submitted GDS's complete Magic RC, with physical MIM devices and interconnect resistances/capacitances. Half-grid import is explicit. Magic retains only Metal3 interface labels in its isolated extraction copy to avoid repeated internal well-name aliases, while native LVS checks the original GDS and its actual body-contact connectivity. No resistance/capacitance threshold omits small parasitics. Source simulation and extraction use the same logical body-net boundary. Distributed substrate resistance/noise and fabrication signoff remain unqualified. The long independent witness is a feasibility layout, not an area optimum.

Electrical Requirements and Scoring

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Quality scoring imposes no fixed degradation allowance. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. Independent source observations define the 100-point electrical baseline without depending on the submitted GDS; reports retain every paired result.

Let x be the post-layout measurement and b the source-circuit measurement under the same conditions:

  • Ratio normalization: maximize with q = x/b and minimize with q = b/x. When a numerical scale s is declared, use (x+s)/(b+s) and its reciprocal, respectively. The scale handles zero values as a normalization floor; it is neither an allowed degradation nor an acceptance bound.
  • Amplitude in dB: maximize with q = 10^((x-b)/20) and minimize with its reciprocal.
  • Target normalization: q = 1/(1+abs(x-b)/s), where s is the declared physical scale. Signed or zero-valued operating points are not divided directly.

Use layout scoring. Each metric takes its worst paired quality q, and the total score is S = 100 * product(q_i ** w_i), with area quality q_area = area_reference / candidate_functional_area. The weights below sum to 1; metric dimensions describe measurements and do not determine weights. Physical or functional rejection scores zero; missing or invalid measurements leave the score unknown, and zero-weight observations must also be valid. Matching source-circuit performance at the reference area scores 100 points; better valid solutions may exceed 100. Weights express quality tradeoffs rather than hard bounds.

The measurements below use the supplied SPICE node and source names. v(n) is a node voltage; i(V) is current flowing into a voltage source, so delivered power uses a negative sign. db(z)=20*log10(abs(z)); mag/abs denote magnitude, and cph denotes continuous phase in radians. find, when, from/to and rise/fall follow the deck's interpolation, window and crossing conventions. SPICE suffixes p/n/u/m/meg/g mean pico/nano/micro/milli/mega/giga. Nested avg, min, max, vecmin/vecmax and deriv represent window averages, extrema and sampled derivatives. Measure each operating condition independently, pair it with the source result under that condition, and take the worst paired quality within each metric group.

output_error_v, recovery_up_v, recovery_down_v use saturating_ratio: q = 2(b+s)/(b+x+2s), where x is candidate error, b is paired source error and s is the positive scale below. Source-equivalent error gives q=1; improvement approaches the upper limit 2 with diminishing returns. s retains the declared units and numeric-floor meaning. Normalize each condition before taking the worst quality; other normalization and functional rules follow their own declarations.

/api/task-guides/ihp-sg13g2.analog-db.am.description_html:
Qu AZC Three-Stage Amplifier Layout Task

Objective

Implement amp_013_qu2017_azc without changing the declared circuit. XM9/XM10 form the PMOS input pair with their bodies tied to the common source net019. XM14–XM17 form the active NMOS load around DM_2/net063; XM4/XM5 convert this to net050. XM11 drives net094 and XM12 with the XM6/XM7 mirror drives net057. XM23/XM24 drive net049; XM13/XM18 drive VOUT. The active compensation retains C0 (net063–VOUT), C1 (net051–vss), C2 (net043–vss), both resistors from net078 to net077/net082, and both resistors from net057 to net051/net043. The entire bias tree and all body relationships remain.

Inputs and Interface

materials/circuit.cdl is the authoritative physical circuit and materials/circuit.spice its equivalent simulation representation; materials/testbench.spice and materials/ac.spice define transient/closed-loop AC and balanced open-loop AC, respectively. This statement is the description input. Ordered interface is vss vdd vinn vinp vout vb1: vss/vdd are supply rails; all other signals, bias/reference and unloaded monitor ports retain netlist connections. /api/task-guides/ihp-sg13g2.analog-db.am.title: Qu AZC Three-Stage Amplifier

/api/task-guides/ihp-sg13g2.analog-db.am.description_html:
Ramos PFC Three-Stage Amplifier Layout Task

Objective

Implement amp_014_ramos_pfc with the supplied fixed topology and dimensions. The PMOS input pair drives the cascoded NMOS branches at dm_2/net063; the voutn mirror produces net050. XM10 and the XM21/XM22 mirror drive net049, while XM11/XM23 drive the single-ended output. Both compensation paths remain: 63 pF from net050 to vout and 25 pF from net050 to net049. The vb3/vb4 bias network is retained. Do not replace the circuit, delete compensation, or add a servo. The circuit contains 24 logical MOS groups with the upstream W, L, multiplicity and four-terminal connections. PMOS groups XM8 and XM9 both have source and body on net31; other PMOS bodies connect to vdd, and NMOS bodies connect to vss.

Inputs and Interface

materials/circuit.cdl is the authoritative logical circuit with native PDK model bindings, materials/circuit.spice its simulation representation, materials/testbench.spice defines closed-loop observations, and materials/ac.spice defines balanced differential AC excitation. Ordered ports are vss vdd vinn vinp vout net1: ground, supply, negative/positive inputs, single-ended output and an external bias-current pull-down. Bias, input drive, feedback connections and loads are external test fixtures. Implement the compensation capacitors and physical body contacts. Body contacts are layout connectivity and are not additional logical circuit devices.

Operating Conditions

IHP SG13G2, nominal TT/typical, 27 C, supply 1.5 V, input reference 0.4 V, external current sink 2.4e-05 A to vss, and 10 pF output load. Use the fixed IHP LV binding at 1.5 V, adapting the authored 1.8 V stimulus to the LV process rail; retain its bias current and input reference. Round W/L to 5 nm (the supplied integer-micrometre sizes are unchanged). The closed-loop deck ties vinn directly to vout, drives vinp with a +100 mV pulse starting at 20 us (100 ns rise/fall, 80 us high duration), and runs to 200 us with 10 ns maximum steps, Gear order 2, reltol=1e-5, abstol=1 pA, vntol=10 nV. Transient starts from the solved DC point; this is not a zero-state supply-ramp startup test. High and return windows are 80–100 and 180–200 us.

AC sweeps 200 points per decade from 1 Hz to 1 GHz. The differential-mode deck retains output DC feedback through a 1 TH inductor and isolates the bias node from AC through a 1 F capacitor to ground; vinp/vinn use balanced +0.5/-0.5 V small-signal excitation. Input common-mode residual amplitude and DC feedback error must both be <=1 uV. These are external small-signal bias fixtures, not physical compensation; an independent closed-loop deck measures actual follower response and does not call a voltage-transfer estimate a loop return ratio.

Physical Requirements

Supply a GDS <=64 MiB with top cell amp_014_ramos_pfc, within 20000 by 2000 um (the task's artifact-size/outline bounds). Native DRC, strict named-interface LVS and functional-area measurement must pass; no marker waivers apply. Preserve MOS models, gate lengths, parallel-equivalent widths (W*m), logical body connections and the two native compensation-capacitor bindings. Electrically equivalent unit arrays, multiple gate fingers and shared diffusion are allowed when native LVS verifies them. Sharing a well is allowed only for bodies on the same logical net. Physically connect each well/substrate region to its declared body net through DRC-compliant contacts; contact count, placement and geometry are layout choices. No particular reference-array partition or isolated well per unit is required. Functional layers in the published task include active, implant, wells, gates, contacts, passive plates, vias and routing; annotation/text-only layers are excluded. IHP native main and maximal DRC use the pinned PDK block profiles, with chip-level density and antenna disabled. The two native MIM bindings use 51.18 um square plates with m=16 and 48.74 um square plates with m=7, giving nominal 62.9964384 pF and 24.9982586 pF at the stated typical model. LVS connects actual tap regions to their wells/substrate before comparing the four-terminal logical MOS; it does not compare a prescribed tap inventory. Source simulation uses the same logical body boundary and native MIM models as candidate extraction. Magic extracts the candidate devices, junction geometry and distributed interconnect RC. This is not distributed substrate or RF/EM extraction. Candidate-derived Magic distributed RC feeds every post-layout job.

Electrical Requirements and Scoring

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Quality scoring imposes no fixed degradation allowance. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. Independent source observations remain required evidence. The explicit quality targets below supply scoring anchors; otherwise the paired source value is used. Reports retain every paired result.

Let x be the post-layout measurement and b the declared quality target, or the same-condition source measurement when no target is declared:

  • Ratio normalization: maximize with q = x/b and minimize with q = b/x. When a numerical scale s is declared, use (x+s)/(b+s) and its reciprocal, respectively. The scale handles zero values as a normalization floor; it is neither an allowed degradation nor an acceptance bound.
  • Amplitude in dB: maximize with q = 10^((x-b)/20) and minimize with its reciprocal.
  • Target normalization: q = 1/(1+abs(x-b)/s), where s is the declared physical scale. Signed or zero-valued operating points are not divided directly.

Use layout scoring. First compute each metric's raw quality q from the worst paired condition, with raw area quality q_area = area_target / candidate_functional_area. Credit c_i = min(1, q_i) for every positively weighted metric, then compute S = 100 * product(c_i ** w_i). The weights sum to 1 and the score is bounded by 100. An improvement beyond one target cannot compensate for missing another target. Physical or functional rejection scores zero; missing or invalid measurements leave the score unknown, and zero-weight observations must also be valid. Reaching every positively weighted target scores 100; a feasible reference may score far below 100. Weights express quality tradeoffs, not acceptance bounds.

late_error_v, return_error_v, ripple_v and return_ripple_v use saturating_ratio. Candidate error x, declared target (or paired source) b and the positive scale s below define q = 2(b+s)/(b+x+2s). Equality to the anchor gives raw q=1; decreasing error approaches raw quality 2, while credited quality stays at 1. The scale retains its declared unit and numerical-floor meaning. Normalize each condition before taking the worst paired quality; other metrics retain their declared normalization and functional requirements.

Metric Definition Unit Treatment
gain_db, gain_10khz_db Balanced differential Vout/(Vinp−Vinn) magnitude at 1 Hz and 10 kHz dB Response, source-paired db20 maximize
closed_gain_10khz_db Actual unity-follower transfer at 10 kHz dB Response target, 6 dB scale
output_v DC follower output V Bias target, 1.5 V scale
power_w DC power drawn from VDD W Supply, inverse ratio, 1 pW floor
mean_power_w Mean supply power over 20–200 us W Supply, inverse ratio, 1 pW floor
late_error_v, return_error_v Mean absolute tracking error in high/return window V Saturating quality for late error; return error diagnostic
ripple_v, return_ripple_v Full output peak-to-peak range in high/return window V Diagnostic
high_v, low_v Window means V Diagnostic
bias_v External bias port DC voltage V Diagnostic
output_min_v, output_max_v Full-transient extrema V Diagnostic
dc_feedback_error_v Absolute DC voltage across the external feedback inductor V Measurement-validity check, 0–1 uV
fixture_cm_max Maximum residual common-mode AC drive V Measurement-validity check, 0–1 uV

All measurements must be finite and complete. Supply power, absolute errors and amplitude ranges must obey their nonnegative physical definitions. The common-mode test-apparatus bound validates differential excitation, rather than DUT common-mode regulation. The DC feedback bound excludes failure of the isolated bias solve. Both apparatus checks apply to source and candidate simulation before scoring. These are this task's hard electrical requirements; upstream paper targets are not acceptance bounds. Window error and ripple do not establish settling or periodic steady state; no phase margin, unity-gain crossing, settling time, CMRR, noise, PVT or mismatch performance is claimed.

Error metrics use saturating normalization 2*(b+s)/(b+x+2*s), with the quality anchor and scale declared below. This differs from an unbounded inverse ratio. Zero-weight ripple, return error, bias and closed-loop gain remain diagnostics; the response integral separately scores dynamic quality. Capability coefficient 7 is independent of the score.

Quality targets and weights

The area quality target is 70000 um2. It is an integration budget, not a hard limit or a proven process minimum.

The 23 fixed MIM plates occupy 58539.3916 um2. A 70000 um2 integration budget allocates about 84% to those plates, leaving 11460.6084 um2 for enclosures, MOS devices, body contacts and interconnect; it is not a minimum-area theorem. Area carries 35%, 100 ppm step-referred late accuracy 15%, the worst bilateral normalized response integral 20%, 10 kHz gain 15%, DC gain 10% and mean power 5%. The response integral removes each final plateau offset, so dynamic response and static accuracy are distinct. Repeated return offset, ripple and operating-point summaries remain diagnostic.

response_time_s takes the worse normalized absolute-error integral: integrate abs(v(vout)-high_v)/0.1 over 20.1–100 us, or abs(v(vout)-low_v)/0.1 over 100.2–180 us. The existing high/return means supply the final plateau values. The 75 ns response-integral budget is a layout-delay quality target under the declared 100 mV step and 10 pF load; it is not an acceptance threshold. Removing each plateau offset isolates dynamic response from the separately scored static error. This finite-window integral is in seconds; it is not a threshold-crossing settling time and does not establish periodic steady state.

Metric Quality anchor Unit Scale Weight
functional_area 70000 um2 — 0.35
late_error_v 1e-05 V 1e-06 0.15

Physical checks and the declared functional bounds must pass. Quality scoring imposes no fixed degradation allowance. Each source_* job and its corresponding candidate extracted circuit use exactly the same testbench, model resources, parameters, loads and measurement windows. Independent source observations remain required evidence. The explicit quality targets below supply scoring anchors; otherwise the paired source value is used. Reports retain every paired result.

Let x be the post-layout measurement and b the declared quality target, or the same-condition source measurement when no target is declared:

  • Ratio normalization: maximize with q = x/b and minimize with q = b/x. When a numerical scale s is declared, use (x+s)/(b+s) and its reciprocal, respectively. The scale handles zero values as a normalization floor; it is neither an allowed degradation nor an acceptance bound.
  • Amplitude in dB: maximize with q = 10^((x-b)/20) and minimize with its reciprocal.

Use layout scoring. First compute each metric's raw quality q from the worst paired condition, with raw area quality q_area = area_target / candidate_functional_area. Credit c_i = min(1, q_i) for every positively weighted metric, then compute S = 100 * product(c_i ** w_i). The weights sum to 1 and the score is bounded by 100. An improvement beyond one target cannot compensate for missing another target. Physical or functional rejection scores zero; missing or invalid measurements leave the score unknown, and zero-weight observations must also be valid. Reaching every positively weighted target scores 100; a feasible reference may score far below 100. Weights express quality tradeoffs, not acceptance bounds.

late_error_v, return_error_v, ripple_v and return_ripple_v use saturating_ratio. Candidate error x, declared target (or paired source) b and the positive scale s below define q = 2(b+s)/(b+x+2s). Equality to the anchor gives raw q=1; decreasing error approaches raw quality 2, while credited quality stays at 1. The scale retains its declared unit and numerical-floor meaning. Normalize each condition before taking the worst paired quality; other metrics retain their declared normalization and functional requirements.

Ordered ports are vss vdd vinn vinp vout net1: ground, supply, negative/positive inputs, single-ended output and an external bias-current pull-down. sections.Objective: Implement amp_014_ramos_pfc with the supplied fixed topology and dimensions. The PMOS input pair drives the cascoded NMOS branches at dm_2/net063; the voutn mirror produces net050. XM10 and the XM21/XM22 mirror drive net049, while XM11/XM23 drive the single-ended output. Both compensation paths remain: 63 pF from net050 to vout and 25 pF from net050 to net049. The vb3/vb4 bias network is retained. Do not replace the circuit, delete compensation, or add a servo. The circuit contains 24 logical MOS groups with the upstream W, L, multiplicity and four-terminal connections. PMOS groups XM8 and XM9 both have source and body on net31; other PMOS bodies connect to vdd, and NMOS bodies connect to vss.
sections.Operating Conditions:
IHP SG13G2, nominal TT/typical, 27 C, supply 1.5 V, input reference 0.4 V, external current sink 2.4e-05 A to vss, and 10 pF output load. Use the fixed IHP LV binding at 1.5 V, adapting the authored 1.8 V stimulus to the LV process rail; retain its bias current and input reference. Round W/L to 5 nm (the supplied integer-micrometre sizes are unchanged). The closed-loop deck ties vinn directly to vout, drives vinp with a +100 mV pulse starting at 20 us (100 ns rise/fall, 80 us high duration), and runs to 200 us with 10 ns maximum steps, Gear order 2, reltol=1e-5, abstol=1 pA, vntol=10 nV. Transient starts from the solved DC point; this is not a zero-state supply-ramp startup test. High and return windows are 80–100 and 180–200 us.

AC sweeps 200 points per decade from 1 Hz to 1 GHz. The differential-mode deck retains output DC feedback through a 1 TH inductor and isolates the bias node from AC through a 1 F capacitor to ground; vinp/vinn use balanced +0.5/-0.5 V small-signal excitation. Input common-mode residual amplitude and DC feedback error must both be <=1 uV. These are external small-signal bias fixtures, not physical compensation; an independent closed-loop deck measures actual follower response and does not call a voltage-transfer estimate a loop return ratio.
